cards.explanation: The answer is Noah. He's the last name in that first run of verses: "Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech, Noah." (1 Chronicles 1:3) He's the man who went into the ark (Genesis 7:7). Ten names in three verses, friends, and Noah is the one at the end.

The answer is Japheth. The verse says, "The sons of Noah: Shem, Ham, and Japheth." (1 Chronicles 1:4) Three sons, and from here the whole list branches out like a family reunion that keeps getting bigger. Japheth is the one who comes third.

The answer is Abraham. The line from Shem ends with "…Abram (that is, Abraham)." (1 Chronicles 1:27) Same man, and the verse says so itself. After all those names, a familiar one feels like spotting a friend in a crowded room.
The answer is Isaac and Ishmael. "The sons of Abraham were Isaac and Ishmael." (1 Chronicles 1:28) The book gives it in one short line and moves on. Both of them get their own family lists coming up.
The answer is Esau and Israel. "Abraham was the father of Isaac. The sons of Isaac: Esau and Israel." (1 Chronicles 1:34) The list lines up Esau's family first, so keep your eyes open, friends.

The answer is the Israelites. The verse says: "These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the Israelites…" (1 Chronicles 1:43) Edom had kings first. The book just lays that out and keeps walking.
